SddReconcile.keywords: reconcile, fix, sync-from-code, drift, spec-probe, bug-vs-spec-defect, problem-class, blast-radius, back-sync, sdd-reconcile
SddReconcile.Mission:
Restore the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle after it desynced, then prove the repaired path. A separate skill (`/sdd-reconcile`) activates one of two modes: - **fix** — a finding / bug / review drove it: the spec is presumed right until the probe proves a spec defect. - **from-code** — code ran ahead of the spec: code is evidence, not automatic authority to rewrite the design.
The probe (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`) classifies ownership, problem class, blast radius, and whether a spec delta is semantic. Remediation then follows its real owner: task-owned code always becomes a new ticket Round; semantic design changes go through the artifact-kind authoring flow, independent semantic review, and operator approval #1 before implementation; only genuinely task-free non-semantic metadata with an exact verifier may use the bounded direct path.
Input — findings / a bug / a review, OR "I changed code, formalize it". Output — merged design when design changed, reopened/created tasks when code must move, tracker state owned by ordinary execute, and one non-duplicated evidence chain for the chosen path.
SddReconcile.ContextExpectation: Reconcile adds only one mechanical command beyond the authoring/execute flows it delegates to: bounded-direct verification runs exact `npx gennady sdd-check --all `. STEP_3 freezes `` and STEP_5 records the literal result in `DIRECT_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT`; no runtime `--help` probe or argument inference is allowed.
SddReconcile.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, QUESTION_RULE_SLIM
`FLOW_VERSION=v1` migration and runtime `EXECUTION_READY=no` remediation can dwarf a narrow request. Size only those broad actions to the task's own blast radius: a narrow owning spec edit may proceed without migrating unrelated legacy tasks or installing unrelated runtime gates. Each `AUTHORING_SCOPE` fact is different: it is a target-specific structural proof and is binding whenever scaffold would create tickets. A red authoring fact blocks scaffold but never blocks the named owning spec flow that repairs the evidence. Product execution always consumes `EXECUTION_READY`; only the exact active GATE_QUEUE setup phase receives its typed exemption.
Any reported problem, bug, or freeform change is first a question about the spec, not a line to patch. Before reconciling, establish three things against the spec: - **Bug or spec-defect?** Does the code violate a correct spec (→ fix the code), or is the code right and the spec was wrong (→ fix the spec and cascade downstream)? This decides which corner of the spec ⟷ code ⟷ task triangle moves. - **The class.** Judging by the spec + this problem, where else does the same class occur? One report is a symptom — scan the closed-world inventory / contracts for siblings (`orient`). - **The blast radius.** From the diff, what else did the change touch that must be re-examined?
Patch only the symptom and you have not done SDD — the spec mediates everything, so reconcile at the right level and propagate.
Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.
Every fix routes through the task that owns the affected file — ownership is resolved from the artifacts, before classification. `@tasks: -[, ...]` in a file header names the owning task(s). Files matching `*.task.-.md` (co-located under `specs/`) are tickets — the Task-ID is in the filename. Files matching `*.1-spec.md` / `*.spec.md` are spec files — linked to a scope, not a single task. Index files (`*.2-tasks.md` / `*.3-tasks.md`, `specs/2-tasks.md` / `specs/3-tasks.md`) are global artifacts, owned by no task. The resulting file → [Task-IDs] map is what routes fixes per `AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`. A resolvable code owner is binding: every code finding routes to that ticket's new Round. Missing or ambiguous ownership does not mean "direct-fix"; recover/create a ticket, or route a semantic ownership gap through authoring first.
A reported symptom is an entry point, never the class. Every finding MUST be classified BEFORE any edit: bug vs spec-defect, ownership, semantic vs editorial spec impact, action category (bounded-direct / authoring-flow / task-reopen / ticket-create-or-recover), the full problem class, and the blast radius. Code carrying a resolvable `@tasks:` owner ALWAYS routes to a newly appended Round in that ticket, even for a one-line fix; size never authorizes a direct patch. A semantic spec change ALWAYS routes through the artifact-kind authoring flow, independent semantic review, and operator approval #1 lifecycle before implementation. Direct editing is reserved for genuinely task-free, non-semantic metadata with a frozen target-set and a known exact verifier. A fix applied without this classification is a symptom patch, not SDD.
Multiple scattered changes with one shared intent (a mass rename, a parameter added across call sites) MUST be grouped into a single logical task. Per-item entries are noise.
Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.
Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).
When reopening a task ticket, append to Execution Log:
``` ### Round N — , fix:
| Phase | Kind | Status | Target Files | Deps | |-------|-------|--------|-------------|------| | P | fix | [ ] | | — | | P | test | [ ] | | P | ```
Allocate concrete next-unused PhaseIDs in the ticket; placeholders are not valid written output. Every task-owned code finding, including a one-line bug, appends a new Round with at least one concrete `fix` PhaseID and one dependent concrete `test` PhaseID. Multiple findings sharing one owner may share that Round, but none may bypass it.
Set ticket Meta Status → `[ ] TODO`. Update `Reopens: `. Sync tracker: the owning `*.3-tasks.md` row → `[ ] TODO`; parent rollups (scope and `specs/3-tasks.md`) → adjust counts.
Every reconcile branch ends with evidence owned by that branch, never a generic duplicate tail: - ordinary execute supplies its per-ticket sync, phase gates, per-group audit, and code-review results; - a semantic spec-only change supplies independent semantic review plus a current human-readable approval #1 marker after operator approval; - a bounded direct metadata correction supplies `DIRECT_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT` for its frozen target-set and exact dedicated command. Missing or red evidence routes back to its owning flow. Never dispatch a second audit/code-review or claim an unexecuted bare tool name as verification.
SddReconcile.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INPUT` | Neither findings / bug nor a code change to reconcile | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Cannot tell fix from from-code — ask the operator | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the reconcile plan | | `H_CLASSIFICATION_UNCONFIRMED` | The dispatched probe did not return ownership, problem class, blast radius, and semantic/editorial verdict | | `H_DIRECT_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE` | A proposed direct edit is task-owned, semantic, has no frozen bounded target-set, or lacks an exact dedicated verifier | | `H_SPEC_KIND_UNRESOLVED` | A semantic spec finding cannot be mapped uniquely to scope, module, infrastructure, or interface authoring | | `H_SPEC_REVIEW_NOT_APPROVED` | Semantic spec authoring did not return approval #1 over independently reviewed actual bytes | | `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL` | The evidence owned by the chosen remediation path is missing or red |

Step.Action: Findings / bug / review present → `fix`. Code already changed / "formalize what I coded" / drift → `from-code` (`AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`; ambiguous → `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE`).

Step.Goal: Clear the FLOW_VERSION/READINESS preflight gate before mapping the affected area.
Step.Action: Use the `FLOW_VERSION` / `READINESS` fields from the `sdd-state` snapshot already produced by the skill's GATHER step; do not call `sdd-state` or `sdd-task` again here. Size the gate to this request's own blast radius (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`): v1 intersecting legacy task layout → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/migration-v1-v2.directive.xml")`; not-ready and this reconcile needs a missing gate → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/readiness.directive.xml")`; otherwise record the out-of-scope state in one line and continue.

Intent-search the specs for the area in play and read the current diff. Resolve the finite set of affected specs, code files, tickets, and trackers; inspect only their ownership headers and linked artifacts. This target picture is the probe boundary, not permission to scan or repair unrelated repository state.

Step.Goal: Probe the spec against the problem (`AX_PROBLEM_PROBES_SPEC`).
Step.Action: Dispatch the critic on the affected spec, seeded with the finding, to return all four fields: bug vs spec-defect; the full repeated problem class; blast radius; and whether every proposed spec edit is semantic or strictly editorial. The critic MUST be an actually dispatched subagent. An orchestrator self-probe never satisfies this step. Missing any field is `H_CLASSIFICATION_UNCONFIRMED`; there is no size-based shortcut around the probe.

Step.Goal: Resolve ownership and choose the only legal remediation class before editing (`AX_FIX_CLASSIFICATION`).
Step.Action:
Build the ownership map first (`AX_TASK_RESOLUTION`): for every affected code file, read its header and resolve every `@tasks: -[, ...]` to exactly one ticket path. For every spec, resolve its canonical artifact kind and scope. Missing or ambiguous code ownership is never permission for a direct edit.
Classify every finding into exactly one category: - **task-reopen** — ANY code finding with a resolvable `@tasks:` owner: bug, contract violation, missing test, BDD mismatch, or review finding. Always append a new Round per `AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`, even for a one-line fix. Allocate concrete next-unused PhaseIDs for at least one `fix` phase and its dependent regression `test` phase; set ticket Meta Status and its owning tracker row to `[ ] TODO`, update `Reopens`, and hand ordinary execute the ticket. No task-owned code path may enter bounded-direct. - **semantic-spec-update** — any change to GOAL, requirements, observable behaviour, contracts, inventory, architecture, dependencies, BDD acceptance, risks, or Decision Log meaning. Route by artifact kind to authoring and complete independent semantic review plus approval #1 before any scaffold, ticket reopen, or execute handoff (`AX_SPEC_LIFECYCLE`). - **editorial-spec-correction** — spelling, formatting, or a mechanical link correction whose already-defined target and meaning do not change. Record an explicit `semantic: no` rationale. Any GOAL or behavioural delta reclassifies it as semantic; editorial must never smuggle one. - **bounded-direct** — only canonical task-free SDD tracker/index metadata, or the editorial spec correction above, when a literal target-set and the dedicated `sdd-check --all` command can be frozen before editing. Code, tickets, semantic content, and unowned executable artifacts are forbidden here. - **ticket-create-or-recover** — unowned code, a missing/ambiguous owner, or any no-task artifact without the bounded-direct contract. Recover a matching ticket when one exists; otherwise create/scaffold one from the owning merged spec. Never patch it directly.

Step.Goal: Materialize the remediation order and exact evidence owner.
Step.Action:
Group findings sharing one intent without crossing owners (`AX_GROUPING_REDUCES_NOISE`). The plan records, per item: - task-reopen: ticket path, new Round number, concrete fix/test PhaseIDs, exact Target Files, dependency from test to fix, and tracker row changing to TODO; - semantic-spec-update: one artifact kind and authoring directive, the integrated bundle that must merge, then the post-merge disposition (`spec-only`, reopen existing tasks, or scaffold uncovered implementation); - bounded-direct: the ordered literal `` and exactly one command per `AX_TOOL_INVOCATION`, npx gennady sdd-check --all , where `` is `specs/` for one editorial spec correction or `` for canonical tracker/index metadata. Freeze both before editing; no other direct verifier is implied; - ticket-create-or-recover: owning merged spec plus recovered/new ticket identity.
Reconcile any genuinely new entity through the existing orient result (`AX_REUSE_FIRST`) and fill the plan's Reuse rationale when the result is JUSTIFY. Present only this delta in `PLAN_TABLE_FORMAT`.

Step.Goal: Obtain operator agreement on the delta (`AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT`).
Step.Action: Ask through `QUESTION_RULE_SLIM` once for only the new or unresolved plan delta. Preserve every already accepted classification/choice without restating or re-asking it; batch independent unresolved choices. Warn only about newly discovered class/blast-radius impact (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`). Stop while awaiting the answer. Rejected → `H_OPERATOR_REJECT`; rejection is not completion and does not create hidden resume state.

Step.Goal: Apply through the remediation owner, preserving design-before-code order.

Action.LogicSwitch:
- WHEN **task-reopen** → append the planned new Round to every owning ticket exactly per `AX_REOPEN_FORMAT`; write its concrete fix and dependent test PhaseIDs, set Meta Status and tracker row to TODO, update parent rollups and `Reopens`, then `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/execute.directive.xml")` for those tickets as an ordinary batch. Reconcile never edits the task-owned code itself and never requests a reconcile-only audit; execute owns phase work, tracker sync, audit, and code-review.
- WHEN **semantic-spec-update** → route the approved delta to exactly one owning authoring flow: canonical product/library scope → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/scope.directive.xml")`; module spec → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/module.directive.xml")`; infrastructure spec → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/infra.directive.xml")`; interface spec → `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interface.directive.xml")`. Unknown or mixed kind without one owning flow is `H_SPEC_KIND_UNRESOLVED`. The selected authoring flow writes the ordinary V2 artifact and MUST run one `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/review-lifecycle.directive.xml")` for its complete bundle. Require its independent verdict and operator approval #1 with a current marker; missing proof is `H_SPEC_REVIEW_NOT_APPROVED`. Only AFTER that proof may implementation move: reopen impacted existing tickets with new concrete fix/test phases and hand ordinary execute; for uncovered implementation load `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/scaffold.directive.xml")`, whose actual-ticket review and approval #2 precede ordinary execute. Interface changes first route implementation through their owning product/library module authoring; they never create a flat interface scaffold. No implementation impact ends as the merged spec-only branch.
- WHEN **bounded-direct** → recheck that every frozen path is genuinely task-free and the approved edit remains editorial/mechanical. Edit only ``, then run the one frozen exact command integrityCheck ToolCall below once. Preserve its literal output and exit code in `DIRECT_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT`. Any path drift, semantic delta, nonzero exit, or missing literal output is `H_DIRECT_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE`; restore the plan to ticket-create-or-recover rather than substituting a lighter command. npx gennady sdd-check --all Inputs : =exact dedicated root frozen for the bounded-direct target-set in STEP_3. Use integrityCheck.
- WHEN **ticket-create-or-recover** → recover the matching ticket or load `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/scaffold.directive.xml")` against the owning already-merged spec to create one. Give it concrete phases and then let scaffold/ordinary execute own implementation. If there is no owning merged spec, reclassify through semantic authoring first; never directly edit the orphan artifact.

Step.Action:
- task-reopen or ticket-create-or-recover → consume ordinary execute's per-ticket sync and phase gates plus each affected group's audit `PASS` / `PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` and code-review outcome. Missing group evidence returns to ordinary execute for that group. - semantic spec-only → consume independent review plus operator approval #1 evidence. - semantic spec plus implementation → require approval #1 to precede the ordinary execute evidence above. - bounded-direct → require the exact `DIRECT_VERIFICATION_RECEIPT` frozen in STEP_3.
Do not run a catch-all second audit/code-review or a duplicate sync/check tail. Any missing/red owned evidence is `H_VERIFICATION_FAIL`. Carry non-blocking code-review proposals into `FIX_SUMMARY_FORMAT`.
Then report the outer result. If task recovery or implementation remains, hand the exact ticket/spec paths to the next ordinary owner. Any blocker, red evidence, unresolved proposal, or operator deferral stops with a concrete resume command. A fully verified spec-only or bounded-direct branch reports completion. All continuation state is in artifacts and Git.

ChatOutput.Contract:
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — an italic blockquote (`> _…_`), 2–3 sentences max: the task retold in the agent's own words plus the single riskiest assumption, linked by wording to the question that resolves it; never a restate of already-settled content — only what is NEW or could be misread (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; if the decision is a flow (data moving, state transitions, start/stop conditions), add a small ASCII diagram — the one place a fenced block is allowed in this message, at most one per message ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_RULE_SLIM` (full format with worked examples lives in `QUESTION_FORMAT`, in the interview / vision directives) ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.

Shown to operator at STEP_3. Compact table per category. Operator may edit. Carries a "Reuse rationale" column/slot — filled per `AX_REUSE_FIRST` whenever an item introduces a new entity/type/method/contract: the JUSTIFY-level one-line rationale for why the existing surface was insufficient (reuse/extend items leave it empty — nothing to justify).

A direct reconcile edit returns this exact evidence block:
``` DirectVerificationReceipt: target-set: [] command: npx gennady sdd-check --all exit: 0 output: ```
The target-set is frozen before editing and contains only canonical task-free SDD tracker/index metadata paths, or one canonical spec path proven editorial. `` is `specs/` for that editorial spec or `` for tracker/index metadata. The command is selected before editing and run exactly once after the edit. Missing output, nonzero exit, a changed target-set, an edit outside it, or an artifact without this dedicated verifier invalidates the direct path and routes to ticket recovery/creation instead.

``` ## ✅ sdd-reconcile complete
Direct fixes: N applied ✅ → 🔍 receipt: target-set= · command= · exit=0
Spec updates: N applied ✅ → · authoring= · approval1=APPROVED
Tasks reopened: N 🔄 TSK-NN — Round N: · phases=, → ordinary execute 🔄 TSK-MM — Round N: · phases=, → ordinary execute
🔍 path evidence: ``` Omit any section whose count is 0. Every file changed on disk MUST appear under exactly one section — a summary whose counts are all zero while the diff is non-empty is a defective summary.
